cards.design_implication: If the system design aims to maximize alignment with the predicted high-probability scenario (80%), it may prioritize modeling assumptions or observational selection criteria consistent with isolated binary evolution and stable mass transfer, rather than common-envelope events.
does_not_establish: The exact parameters of the 'default evolutionary model' beyond the star formation metallicity spread and mean metallicity scaling mentioned elsewhere in the abstract.
Causal mechanisms independent of the stated model assumptions.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Intriguingly, this default model predicts that 80 per cent of the approximately one binary black hole merger per day that will be detectable at design sensitivity will have formed through isolated binary evolution with only dynamically stable mass transfer, i.e. without experiencing a common-envelope event.
limitations: The prediction is specific to the 'default evolutionary model' described in the abstract.
The percentage applies to mergers detectable at 'design sensitivity' with a rate of approximately one per day.
cards.statement: The default evolutionary model predicts that 80 per cent of detectable binary black hole mergers will have formed through isolated binary evolution with only dynamically stable mass transfer.
